hook: Miles Brundage is an AI policy researcher who spent six years at OpenAI working on how the world should prepare for increasingly capable AI systems. He holds a BA in political science from George Washington University and a PhD in the Human and Social Dimensions of Science and Technology from Arizona State University, completed in 2019, with earlier stints at ARPA-E and the Institute for Human and Machine Cognition. From 2016 to 2018 he was a research fellow at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute before joining OpenAI in 2018 as a research scientist on its policy team. Over six years there he rose to head of policy research and then senior advisor for AGI readiness, leading the company's external red-teaming program and developing its first system cards for documenting model capabilities. He left OpenAI in October 2024, saying he wanted to influence AI's development from outside industry, and went on to found AVERI, a nonprofit focused on independent AI policy research, while advising organizations including the Institute for Progress, CNAS, Epoch AI and RAND.

standing.watch: What is unresolved in the records is the litigation itself. Each of the OpenAI cases is recorded only as filed, with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, so no outcome, ruling or settlement appears. The records give dates for some filings, including Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC and JIANG v. Beyond the cases, the records note that Brundage founded AVERI and advises several organizations, but they do not describe what those bodies will do next. On these records, the coming developments are the pending OpenAI matters and whatever follows from his post-OpenAI work.

standing.standing: Miles Brundage stands in the records as a former OpenAI executive and an AI policy researcher, having spent six years at the company from 2018 to 2024 and risen to head of policy research and then senior advisor for AGI readiness. He led OpenAI's external red-teaming program and developed its first system cards for documenting model capabilities. He left OpenAI in October 2024, saying he wanted to influence AI's development from outside industry, and founded AVERI, a nonprofit focused on independent AI policy research. He also advises organizations including the Institute for Progress, CNAS, Epoch AI and RAND, and is listed as a non-resident senior fellow at the Institute for Progress. His influence in the records rests on that OpenAI tenure and on the advisory roles he now holds.
